title: Kasumi Courier: A 90s-style cyberpunk delivery game (browser demo update)
author: burgric
selftext:
Hi folks, I thought this community would be the right place to get some good feedback on a game I  just released.

Kasumi Courier is a first-person cyberpunk delivery game. You start out on a moped, riding through a rain-soaked neon city from 22:00 till dawn, delivering parcels against the clock.

I released the full game a few days ago on itch and have just uploaded a browser demo version. It can be played here:

[https://amberglowgames.itch.io/kasumi-courier](https://amberglowgames.itch.io/kasumi-courier)

Originally I intended to create a browser game, to see what Claude could do with three.js. As it grew, it eventually became a desktop app. I’m a composer with no programming experience. I've been vibecoding projects for about a year now with Claude (mainly Unity games). I directed and designed most of the game, and Claude (Opus 5.5) on medium wrote the code: about 24,000 lines of JavaScript with three.js, packaged with Electron.

It took about 7 weeks to develop the game. I created a design doc with Claude around mid-September, which included most of the game's features, core loops, a technical plan, a basic narrative outline and development roadmap. This was revised and updated as development progressed.

All the game's models are pixel art drawn in code. I provided Claude with a prompt regarding the visual style, and it created very basic characters, vehicles and buildings which were reviewed and refined over time with further prompts. 

All the music across radio stations/locations was synthesised in code with the Web Audio API. I outlined the stylistic elements and instrumentation of each track, listened to renders and gave notes until I was satisfied. One track in game is my own composition.

The overall design loop was: describe a feature, test it, screenshot what was wrong, repeat. Clipping and z-fighting were frequent issues and I hit my weekly usage limit most weeks. Testing and refining took up most of the time.

Claude wrote most of the writing in game, which I reviewed and edited throughout the process. The branching late game required most attention, as the player can make several major narrative choices.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow and welcome any feedback and suggestions. Thanks for checking it out!

comments.author: Layers3d
comments.body: is the cyberpunk actually cyberpunk or just retro wave aesthetics?

replies.author: burgric
replies.body: Thanks for your feedback :) I went for a retro 80s aesthetic for the city. The characters and their dialogue reflect the cyberpunk/dystopian elements. I've been thinking about updating the vehicles and buildings to be more cyberpunk in appearance so will explore this soon

comments.author: Ausstewa
comments.body: I like the look of it! You’re very close to the Crazy Taxi style of gameplay in a good way. Maybe lean into that more

replies.author: burgric
replies.body: Thanks for your feedback :) it is strange that the few clips in the video feature quiet roads as they are usually busier! I'll record busier streets next time

replies.author: burgric
replies.body: Ha! I had another comment mentioning this game and hadn't heard of it before. Checked it out today. Looked pretty rad!

comments.author: SassyTextDev
comments.body: This is GREAT! Fucking VIBES on this.
